sources.citation: Pozdniakov, Konstantin. 2018. The numeral system of Proto-Niger-Congo: A step-by-step reconstruction (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 2). Berlin: Language Science Press. 439 pp. [HAL hal-02019192]
sources.note: Nothing on Bomwali prosody; Bomwali appears only as numeral forms (p. 14), in the noun-class grouping table of numerals (p. 315) and in the source list (p. 338). Used here as the pointer that identified John Phillips (SIL Congo) as a holder of first-hand Bomwali data. PDF read in the work directory, not kept (secondary, no Bomwali phonology).

sources.citation: Beavon, Keith & Ann Elizabeth Johnson. 2011. Sociolinguistic Survey Among the Ɓekwel. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-045 (November 2011). SIL International. 15 pp. [report of a July 1988 SIL survey in the Moloundou area, East Province, Cameroon; original draft report 1989]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Bomwali appears in sec. 5 (discovered in the Moloundou area, added to the lexicostatistics and comprehension testing), Table 1 (Ɓekwel-Bomwali 83.5% cognate on ~100 words), Table 2 and the Appendix (Ɓekwel speakers' scores on the Bomwali test tape, 'tested with only one Bomwali speaker.. should not necessarily be considered as reliable'), and sec. 6.4 (one or two Bomwali speakers helped fill out a questionnaire). Zero occurrences of tone/tonal/stress/accent/phonology in the whole report; the wordlists themselves are not printed.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). 2009 [page created 2006, data dated 16 Dec 2009]. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Bomwali (Cameroon, Congo). Data supplied by John Phillips, SIL International, Congo; informant Ndjeka Joseph, Ouesso. Leipzig: MPI-EVA,https://lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/Bomwali.htm
sources.note: Wordlist-only data: numerals 1-29, tens to 100, 200, 1000, 2000 transcribed with tone diacritics (e.g. wɔtɔ́ 1, ɓeɓa 2, ɓeláali 3, ɓenâ 4, ɓetáani 5, tʰoobô 6, tʰámalî 7, mwáambi 8 '< Lingala', táani ne ɓinâ 9 '(5+4)', kamɔ 10, mɔkamɔ ɓá 20, káma 100). The acute/circumflex marks imply lexical tone (H and falling) was transcribed, but the page makes NO statement about the tone system or stress; 'Other comments' says only: 'Bomwali has a decimal system. There are loanwords from Lingala.' Tone marks in a numeral list are data, not a statement.
sources.venue: Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Bomwali (Cameroon, Congo)

sources.note: Nothing. The notice (pp. 198-200) lists Gravot's fifteen vocabularies and quotes his observations: D'Zimu, D'Zem, Sangha-Sangha and Gumba 'semblent appartenir à la même famille Bantou' (shared radicals; ma- plural 'Ma-dié, dents, dans les quatre dialectes'; possessive particle 'Ma-pa-badu, pierre de feu en Sangha-Sangha'; 'La numération est décimale en Sangha-Sangha et en Gumba'); the Ba-Yaga (Baka) idioms are excluded from Bantu. Pages 201-219 are a French / 'Bantou' / 'Négrille' comparative vocabulary in plain French-style spelling with no diacritics for tone or accent. Zero occurrences of…

sources.citation: Revue d'ethnographie et de sociologie vol. 2 (1911) [archive.org item revuedethnogr21121911inst] — downloaded to reach Bruel, Georges. 1910-11. Les Populations de la Moyenne Sanga. RES 1: 3-32; 2: 111-125
sources.note: Bruel's text is not in this scan: pp. 111-125 of the 1911 volume are book reviews. The volume does contain Ouzilleau, 'Notes sur la langue des pygmées de la Sanga' (pp. ~76-92), which mentions the 'Bumuali de Ouesso' only as a Fang-related tribe and gives no Bomwali data and nothing on stress. Vol. 1 (1910), with Bruel pp. 3-32, is not on archive.org; Gallica and HathiTrust were blocked.

sources.citation: Bruel, Georges. 1910. Les populations de la moyenne Sanga: les Pomo et les Boumali; (suite) les Babinga; Appendice: Vocabulaires. Revue d'ethnographie et de sociologie 1: 3-32, 111-125. [read as the HTRC Extracted Features 2.0 page-level token inventory of HathiTrust volume uc1.c2658101 (v.1, 1910), seq 15-61 and 145-166; file placed in the held mirror by reader ling-altcopy on 2026-09-21, read here]
sources.note: Token census only (word order not recoverable): the Bruel pages (seq 17-52 = pp. 3-32; seq 149-166 = pp. 111-125 with the 'Appendice: Vocabulaires', Pomo and Lino columns) contain no token beginning accent/toniq/syllab/intonat/prosod; the language passage (seq 46-47, ca. pp. 26-27) carries only 'langue(s)', 'dialectes', 'parlees', 'vocabulaires', 'Bantou', and p. 13 (seq 25) 'prononce', 'mots'. So the 1910 article classifies the speech as Bantu and prints vocabularies but makes no remark on accent or tone. Confidence limited by the bag-of-words format and scanned quality.

sources.citation: Loyre, Emile. 1909. Les Populations de la Moyenne-Sangha. Questions diplomatiques et coloniales 28(303): 406-420. [archive.org scanned of the whole volume, item questionsdiploma28pariuoft]
